title: Mean - Basic Definition
text: The arithmetic mean is the average of a set of numerical values. It is calculated by adding all values and dividing their sum by the number of values.

title: Mean - Mathematical Definition
text: For values x_1 through x_n, the arithmetic mean is x_bar = (x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_n) / n.

title: Mean - Example
text: For the values 2, 4, 6, and 8, the mean is (2 + 4 + 6 + 8) / 4 = 5.

title: Median - Basic Definition
text: The median is the middle value of a set of observations after the values have been arranged in order.

title: Median - Even-Sized Data Set
text: When a data set contains an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middle values after the observations are ordered.

title: Median - Compared with Mean
text: Unlike the mean, the median is relatively resistant to extreme outliers, so it can be a more representative measure of center for skewed data.

title: Outliers - Basic Definition
text: An outlier is an observation that is unusually far from the other values in a data set.

title: Outliers - Effect on Mean and Median
text: A very large or very small outlier can pull the mean substantially, while the median usually changes much less.

title: Outliers - Example
text: For the values 2, 3, 3, 4, and 100, the value 100 is an extreme outlier. It makes the mean much larger than the median.

title: Population Variance - Basic Definition
text: Population variance measures how far the values in an entire population tend to vary from the population mean.

title: Population Variance - Formula
text: Population variance is sigma squared = sum((x_i - mu)^2) / N, where mu is the population mean and N is the population size.

title: Population Variance - Standard Deviation
text: The population standard deviation is the square root of the population variance.

title: Sample Variance - Basic Definition
text: Sample variance estimates the variability of a population using observations collected from a sample.

title: Sample Variance - Formula
text: Sample variance is s squared = sum((x_i - x_bar)^2) / (n - 1), where x_bar is the sample mean and n is the sample size.

title: Sample Variance - Bessel's Correction
text: Sample variance divides by n - 1 instead of n. This adjustment is called Bessel's correction and helps produce an unbiased estimate of population variance under common assumptions.

title: Independent Events - Basic Definition
text: Two events are independent when knowing that one event occurred does not change the probability of the other event.

title: Independent Events - Formula
text: For independent events A and B, P(A and B) = P(A) times P(B).

title: Independent Events - Example
text: A fair coin toss and a fair six-sided die roll can be treated as independent events because the outcome of the coin toss does not change the probabilities of the die roll.

title: Conditional Probability - Basic Definition
text: Conditional probability is the probability that an event A occurs given that another event B is known to have occurred.

title: Conditional Probability - Formula
text: Conditional probability is P(A given B) = P(A and B) / P(B), provided P(B) is greater than zero.

title: Conditional Probability - Relation to Independence
text: If A and B are independent, knowing that B occurred does not change the probability of A, so P(A given B) equals P(A).

title: Bayes' Rule - Basic Definition
text: Bayes' rule describes how to update the probability of a hypothesis after observing evidence.

title: Bayes' Rule - Formula
text: Bayes' rule is P(A given B) = P(B given A) P(A) / P(B), where P(A) is the prior probability and P(A given B) is the posterior probability.

title: Bayes' Rule - Relation to Conditional Probability
text: Bayes' rule is derived from the definition of conditional probability and allows a conditional probability to be expressed in the reverse direction.

title: Linear Functions - Basic Definition
text: A linear function describes a relationship in which the output changes at a constant rate as the input changes.

title: Linear Functions - Formula
text: A linear function can be written as y = m x + b, where m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.

title: Linear Functions - Example
text: For y = 2x + 3, the slope is 2 and the y-intercept is 3. Every increase of 1 in x produces an increase of 2 in y.

title: Correlation - Basic Definition
text: Correlation measures the strength and direction of an association between two variables, commonly focusing on linear association.

title: Correlation vs. Causation
text: A correlation between two variables does not by itself establish that one variable causes the other. A third variable, coincidence, or other explanation may account for the association.

title: Correlation vs. Causation - Example
text: Ice cream sales and swimming incidents may increase during the same months. This correlation does not mean ice cream causes swimming incidents; warmer weather could influence both.
